question_record.context: During an ongoing hands-on-keyboard attack via the Impacket toolkit, suspicious activity with the `powershell.exe` and `lsass.exe` processes was observed. This indicates a potential attempt by attackers to move laterally across the network to execute commands on other hosts. Attackers often use tools like Impacket in hands-on-keyboard attacks to install ransomware or other malicious payloads onto target devices.
question_record.question: Can you identify the process id, created time and command line of the attempted hidden execution of the dual-purpose tool?
solution: There was ongoing hands-on-keyboard attack via Impacket toolkit initiated by an account with SID `S-2-5-21-571436798-3864380397-1837441745-3206` on 2024-07-04 22:35:01.395957+00:00.

An attempt to hide use of a dual-purpose tool was detected on process with Process ID `5752`, created on 2024-07-06t00:00:01.7155092z, and command line `iy2orr1e.rrg.exe -windowstyle hidden -encodedcommand qwa6afwauwbjahiaaqbwahqacwbcaeuaeabwag8acgb0aeearabgafmavabvagsazqbuafmaaqbnag4aaqbuaemazqbyahqalgbwahmamqa=`.

16.name: Ongoing hands-on-keyboard attack via Impacket toolkit
16.description:
Suspicious execution of a command via Impacket was observed on this device. This tool connects to other hosts to explore network shares and execute commands. Attackers might be attempting to move laterally across the network using this tool. This usage of Impacket has often been observed in hands-on-keyboard attacks, where ransomware and other payloads are installed on target devices.

Corresponding TA for this IOA: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/ff7e4fff-dde3-49be-9a06-7f63a490996d/analystreport

68.name: Attempt to hide use of dual-purpose tool
68.description:
A known public tool, which could also be used for malicious reasons, was observed under an unexpected filename.
This might be an attempt to hide the usage of that tool for malicious purposes.

interpretation.scope: official graph witness, not a proof of causality, actor identity or autonomous planning

steps.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT o.AlertId, o.AlertTitle, o.ObservedAt, o.EntityIndex,
       o.GraphValue AS value, o.RawComponents, o.Roles, o.SourceRowHash,
       i.GraphValue AS matched_input
FROM LTMInputEvidence i
JOIN LTMEntityEvidence o ON o.SourceRowHash = i.SourceRowHash
WHERE i.AlertTitle = %s
  AND i.Concept = 'Account_Name' AND o.Concept = 'Account_SID'
  AND i.GraphValue IN (%s)
ORDER BY o.AlertId, o.SourceRowHash, o.EntityIndex, o.GraphValue, i.GraphValue
LIMIT 501
